input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by Customer to Vendor for any delay in providing a "dependency" — an undefined, potentially minor trigger with no aggregate cap, which could exceed the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Our playbook position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; only service credits or LDs flowing to Customer are acceptable, and no such Customer-payable amount appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 contain no termination fee or penalty). The minimal fix is to delete Section 7.6; if a fixed sum is unavoidable, the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages payable by us for dependency delays, as our playbook does not permit liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer. Vendor's remedies for our delays remain available under the general terms (including relief from delay-related obligations), and if a fixed amount is essential we could instead accept an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages in Section 7.6
